📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the classic Thanksgiving comedy Planes, Trains and Automobiles, hapless hero Del Griffith (played by the late, great John Candy) delivers an emotional riposte to Steve Martin’s uptight ad man Neal Page that stands as a beautifully dignified defense of kindness, empathy and self-love in the face of his own perceived shortcomings.

“You want to hurt me? Go right ahead if it makes you feel any better…I could be a cold, hard cynic like you. But I don’t like to hurt people’s feelings. You think what you want about me, I’m not changing. I… I like me. My wife likes me…because I’m the real article. What you see is what you get.”.

For many of us around the holidays, particularly after a night of excess, Del and Neal’s exchange could read as our internal monologue – your kinder inner voice battling the internal bully who judges your every overindulgence. The jury’s out on whether the kind voice is ever as potent as Del’s is in that moment. But it should be, because when it comes to your health around the holidays, the bully has usually got it wrong.

The truth is, for most of us, one day of immoderation during Thanksgiving is unlikely to matter in the grand scheme. As such, you would do well to avoid the litany of holiday season health myths out there, many of which seem hell-bent on punishing you for taking a day off:.

Like all misinformation, these kinds of medical myths are loud and tend to die hard, but they almost always trade on quick fixes that target the wrong thing.

It has been revealed that A 2020 review of 23 observational studies found that most demonstrated significant weight gain during festive periods, averaging roughly a pound and a half. One of the original studies, a landmark NIH study from 2000, found that much of that weight tends to stick around. So the question is not what you ate on Thanksgiving Thursday and how rapidly you can “undo the damage,” but rather whether the extended holiday season becomes a two-month period where your healthy routine goes out the window. Some things to look out for on that front:.

In a recent development, none of this is a free pass for everyone. If you manage a health condition, you likely have less margin for error, even when talking about a single meal or a drink. Critical factors include timing, sodium intake, alcohol intake, and missed medication. A few non-exhaustive examples:.

Whatever condition you’re managing, the move for all of them remains the same – be prepared. Check your plan with your care team before the holiday, not after, and call them if something feels off afterward.

Industry observers note that technically, feeling good on Black Friday starts on Thursday. A short and light walk after a feast can help smooth out post-meal blood sugar – the earlier the better, ideally within an hour of eating. Staying upright for a couple of hours to help with digestion, particularly if you’re prone to reflux, is also a great idea. If you’re on medication, remember to take it on time. And, at the risk of sounding prudish, and this goes for everyone: try to get to bed at a sensible hour.

Above all else, Thanksgiving is a holiday built around gratitude and kindness, so channel your inner Del Griffith and remember to be both grateful and kind, to yourself and to those around you – evidence suggests that’s also good for your health.

Robin Hough is the Editor-in-Chief of Healthline, and in addition to this regular Letter from the Editor column, he can be found every other Wednesday in our Healthline Wellness Wire newsletter.

#63849. How to Deal With People Who Always Excuse Their Bad Behavior

How to Deal With People Who Always Excuse Their Bad Behavior

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (870 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 21, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.
  • Recent findings suggest that you’ve met them; I’ve met them: folks who seem always critical or controlling, forgetful or unreliable, and often good at apologizing later.
  • You want to be sympathetic and understanding, but over time, it all gets old.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 21, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.

Recent findings suggest that you’ve met them; I’ve met them: folks who seem always critical or controlling, forgetful or unreliable, and often good at apologizing later. But the apology often ends with a comment like, “I guess it’s just the way I am; I’ve been this way my whole life.” Or, “Because I’ve been doing _____ for so long, I guess my brain is wired to think in terms of ___.” Or, “Because I struggle with—ADHD, depression, anxiety, etc.—I can’t always do _____—e.g., not be late or follow through.”.

You want to be sympathetic and understanding, but over time, it all gets old. In your heart of hearts, it starts to feel like a default excuse—their way of dismissing your feelings, of not considering or caring about you, and of leaving you not only frustrated but, at times, even emotionally manipulated.

What’s going on? Why do some people lean on personality weaknesses or mental health diagnoses to explain or excuse what is often simply bad behavior? Here are five common sources:.

Your father-in-law always seems critical of you, but in his mind, he is just expressing his opinion, making conversation, or even being helpful by offering suggestions. Pointing out that you feel criticized doesn’t help—he either thinks you’re being too sensitive or rationalizes it by blaming his ingrained habits: Because I’ve been supervising people my whole life, I guess I’m just wired to see the negative.

For some, it’s understandable to be exhausted from trying to manage their depression, anxiety, ADHD, trauma reactions, etc. They've been through dozens of treatments, dozens of drugs that make minimal change at best, but no real relief. They are left feeling that this is what they have to deal with and, often, that they're sorry it affects you as well.

It has been revealed that this takes resignation to a higher level, where their struggles have solidified into their overall self-concept: I’m not just a person who struggles with high anxiety, but I am an anxious person, or You don’t understand—I have ______. Sometimes these folks can, understandably, seem overly assertive and rigid, or, once they've informed you, expect you to be automatically accepting and accommodating. If you are not, they can swiftly get upset.

Sorry I can’t come into work today, show up for the party, finish my work assignment, or so on because I’m having a flare, I forgot to take my meds, or my _________ is really bad. This goes from explanation to manipulation because they are lying, and their motive is clear: to use their real condition to get what they want. This is often a characterological problem where they lack empathy and use people as tools for their own ends.

Industry observers note that so how should you respond in these situations? At a basic level, it’s about shaping a two-sided relationship where you can only control your side. Here are some suggestions.

If your father-in-law keeps brushing off your comments about his criticism, even though you’ve gently explained how it affects you, it’s time to drill down: Ben, I know your comments come from good intentions, and you probably think I’m being overly sensitive, but I don’t understand how, if you care about me—and I believe you do—you don’t make an effort to stop doing what feels hurtful to me.

One obvious path is to have a conversation about that—the giving up—not as a therapist or as someone trying to fix them, but simply as someone who cares about them and wants to understand why they are so discouraged. Your deeper understanding can help you feel less frustrated and more accepting, and the conversation may help them be more sensitive to you.

Recent findings suggest that time to set boundaries. If you have the clout, call them out on their behavior—require a doctor’s note when they are out sick, or hold them to deadlines at work. If the relationship is more peer-to-peer, do what you need to stop feeling repeatedly taken advantage of: Speak up and tell them how you feel, but more importantly, stop making excuses for them, stop doing the heavy lifting in the relationship, and maybe end it.

Whether it's your dismissive father-in-law, your overly assertive or discouraged friend, or your manipulative employee, they may react negatively to your response, whatever it may be. This is about repairing communication. Here, you work on your side of the relationship by acknowledging their feelings and clarifying what you were trying to convey, without responding in kind or feeling the need to back down. Be sensitive and calm, yet assertive.

Relationships are no longer healthy when they feel out of balance—when you’re not getting enough back for what you give, when you feel used, abused, or simply dismissed. Step back, assess the relationship climate, and advocate for yourself to get what you need.

Is it time to stop making excuses for them and accepting what you get?

Taibbi, R. (2019). Boot camp therapy: Action-oriented approaches to anxiety, anger & depression. Fresh York: Norton.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • September was a good month to be selling a used Tesla Model Y.
  • Americans bought an estimated 48,678 used EVs in October, according to the latest EV Market Monitor from Cox Automotive.
  • Cox says used EV sales rose 4.7% from September to October.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

September was a good month to be selling a used Tesla Model Y. Sales jumped nearly 14% from August, and the Ford Mustang Mach-E did even better. The Chevrolet Equinox EV beat both, though, with a nearly 42% increase. A month later, only one of those three electric crossovers was still gaining buyers: the Chevy.

Americans bought an estimated 48,678 used EVs in October, according to the latest EV Market Monitor from Cox Automotive. That’s up 4.7% from September and 73.2% year over year. Used Tesla sales, meanwhile, fell 5.4% from September, with the Model 3, Model Y, and Model X losing ground.

Cox says used EV sales rose 4.7% from September to October. However, its September report put sales at 47,862 vehicles. October’s total of 48,678 is 816 higher, which is a 1.7% gain; Cox doesn’t explain the discrepancy.

It has been revealed that tesla still dominated the used EV scene, though. The change was one spot down, with Chevrolet moving ahead of Ford into second place. Hyundai and BMW rounded out the top five. The Equinox EV and Blazer EV added to their September gains, while the Kia EV6, Nissan Leaf and Volkswagen ID.4 also found more buyers than in the previous month.

Cox says this is because a growing supply of cars coming off lease is giving shoppers more choices across brands and price points.

In a recent development, that 73% jump over last year deserves a little context. October 2025 was the first full month after the federal EV tax credit ended and Americans bought about 30,000 used EVs. In March, sales hit a record of nearly 43,000. EVs made up 3.3% of U.S. used car sales in October, matching September’s record and up from 2% a year earlier.

Sources indicate that for used EV shoppers, the more useful number might be $36,582. That was the average asking price for a used EV in October, down from $36,767 in September and 1.9% below a year earlier. The Equinox EV, ID.4, Mach-E and Nissan Ariya all got cheaper.

Used Teslas didn’t for a second consecutive month, rising 1.8% to an average of $34,109. Even after that increase, the average used Tesla was listed for about $2,500 less than the average used EV.

Used EVs still carried a $2,236 premium over gas cars and hybrids, up slightly from $2,137 in September. Dealers had 38 days’ worth of used EVs on hand at October’s sales pace, versus 47 days for gas cars and hybrids.

According to recent reports, at October’s sales pace, traditional dealers had enough used Teslas to last 32 days, the shortest supply of any major brand Cox tracked. Cox’s count leaves out Tesla’s own stores. Another study looked at how long each used EV spent on dealer lots in September. The Audi Q4 E-Tron Sportback sold the fastest, and no Tesla made the top ten.

Over on the newly introduced-car side, Americans bought 83,262 EVs in October, down 3.9% from September but up 3% from a year earlier, marking the first year-over-year gain of 2026. EVs’ share of new sales slipped from 6.5% in September to 6.2% last month. The average buyer paid $56,221 for a new EV, even with incentives averaging $6,375 per vehicle. Dealers had 85 days’ supply of new EVs, more than double their used inventory.

October wasn’t all bad for Tesla. While sales of second-hand Model Ys fell, Americans bought 36,366 brand-newly introduced examples, up 9.4% from September. It accounted for nearly 44% of all new EVs sold in the country.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Cincinnati Zoo’s most famous resident Fiona the hippo has died at age 9.
  • “We are in shock at the moment,” Cincinnati Zoo director Dave Jenike said in a statement.
  • Last week, a child’s knit hat entered her enclosure at the Cincinnati Zoo and the almost 10-year-old hippo ate it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Cincinnati Zoo’s most famous resident Fiona the hippo has died at age 9.

“We are in shock at the moment,” Cincinnati Zoo director Dave Jenike said in a statement. “We did not expect this outcome. She fought until she couldn’t anymore. Our animal care team was heroic in their efforts to save her. They did everything possible, but her body couldn’t fight anymore. She was dearly loved by her Zoo family and countless others around the world. Her loss will be felt deeply by so many.”.

Last week, a child’s knit hat entered her enclosure at the Cincinnati Zoo and the almost 10-year-old hippo ate it. Given her size, zookeepers initially thought she’d simply pass the hat, but it remained stuck in her digestive track. She had undergone a colonoscopy using a 9-foot scope and multiple ultrasounds that demonstrated intestinal bunching, indicating her body was trying and expel the hat. Caretakers have continued to give her fluids and sedate her when necessary for tests. Just yesterday, on November 18, the zoo shared a new approach in Fiona’s ongoing treatment: a vibration plate borrowed from a local Ohio horse farm. Fiona could be seen standing on the plate, vocalizing to caretakers.

Industry observers note that “Fiona was such a gift,” mentioned Cincinnati Zoo Executive Chair of the Board Thane Maynard. “I have never known an animal so beloved in all my life. From the day she was born, she was like lightning in a bottle. And, she will be remembered and beloved many years from now.”.

Fiona first captured the internet’s heart in 2017, when she was born six weeks premature. Baby hippos typically weigh about 100 pounds at birth, but tiny Fiona tipped the scales at a mere 29 pounds. She was the smallest known hippo to survive such a low birth weight. As she grew, Fiona took social media and the real world by storm: she photobombed an engagement shoot, had a local ice cream named in her honor, and even starred in her own reality-TV series appropriately called “The Fiona Show.”  Her surprise baby brother Fritz was born in 2022, after their mother’s birth control went “on the fritz.”.

According to recent reports, alpitronic, the company behind IONNA’s fast chargers, is investing nearly $34 million in a new South Carolina factory. It’ll build 400 kW DC fast chargers, plus a 1 megawatt (MW) system that can charge cars and heavy-duty trucks.

The $33.94 million project in Fort Mill is expected to create 70 jobs, the South Carolina Department of Commerce unveiled Wednesday. It’ll be the Bolzano, Italy-based Alpitronic’s first operation in South Carolina, just across the state line from its North American headquarters in Charlotte.

In a recent development, the HYC400 packs up to 400 kW into a single unit. If you’ve stopped at an IONNA Rechargery, you may have already plugged into one.

The HYC1000 works differently. A separate power cabinet can send up to 1 MW across as many as eight vehicles at once, shifting power between them as their charging needs change. Operators can configure it with CCS or NACS plugs for passenger EVs or a Megawatt Charging System (MCS) plug for compatible heavy-duty trucks.

Industry observers note that alpitronic’s 400 kW chargers were already being made in Wisconsin for Mercedes-Benz High-Power Charging in 2024. Alpitronic Americas CEO Patrik Herrnegger mentioned the Fort Mill plant “will put US production under our direct control, bring us closer to our customers, and enable us to serve them more efficiently.”.

The 173,315-square-foot site at 3560 Stateview Blvd. (pictured above) will also house a testing lab, repair operations, a warehouse, logistics space, and offices. South Carolina approved job development credits and awarded York County a $200,000 grant to help pay for building improvements.

#63842. This Hedley Studios Porsche 550 J Is A Shrunken Electric Replica Track Toy

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (670 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Insideevs ↗ Open Full Page

This Hedley Studios Porsche 550 J Is A Shrunken Electric Replica Track Toy

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (670 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Insideevs

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hedley Studios in the UK just came out with a replica Porsche 550 Spyder, which itself isn't a unique idea.
  • I can't tell if the 550 J is a track toy or just a toy, but either way it looks like fun.
  • Like a real 550 Spyder, all of the 550 J's weight is behind the driver.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This is adorable and I want one. Hedley Studios in the UK just came out with a replica Porsche 550 Spyder, which itself isn't a unique idea. There have been Volkswagen-powered 550 Spyder replicas for decades. What sets this one apart are two things: one is that it's only 80% scale, so it's a little fella, and the other is that it's electric. It's called the Porsche 550 J (for Junior) it looks like a blast.

I can't tell if the 550 J is a track toy or just a toy, but either way it looks like fun. At 80% scale, it looks positively bite-sized next to the real one, which was already one of the smallest production road cars you'll ever see. So it's tiny. So much so, in fact, that I struggle to see how two adults can actually fit in its two seats side-by-side. And, as you'd imagine with such a tiny footprint, the 550 J isn't road legal and is only meant for private roads and race track.

Like a real 550 Spyder, all of the 550 J's weight is behind the driver. Two 1.8 kWh battery packs provide the juice at 48 volts, while a single 11 horsepower electric motor drives the rear wheels. It only weighs 728 pounds, so that power should be enough to have some fun with. Add two passengers, though, and its weight can pretty easily pass the half-ton mark. At that point, 11 horses isn't much. However, there is an optional RS pack that bumps it to 21 horsepower. Top speed also jumps from 40 mph to 50 mph.

In a recent development, the RS Pack also adds two more of those 1.8 kWh battery packs, though, which adds another 44 pounds. That weight penalty might be worth it for the range, though. The standard 550 J only has 30 miles of range, while the RS has 50. That isn't a lot but it's enough for a track day. Plus, with such small batteries, the 550 J will charge up quickly. Lap the track a bunch of times, plug it in and have some lunch, and get back to it.

Track days should be fun, too. Bilstein dampers with Eibach springs handle suspension duty, while Brembo brakes do the stopping. The RS model gets Bilstein adjustable coilovers and drilled brake rotors, too. So despite having Power Wheels-levels of horsepower, it has genuine track car handling bits.

Industry observers note that hedley has done an admirable job of making the 550 J look like a real 550 Spyder that was hit with a shrink ray. It's smaller, sure, but you wouldn't know it from photos. Everything about it looks spot on, from every exterior detail of its carbon fiber body, to the interior switchgear, and even the fuel filler cap. It's a very impressive recreation and one that will look fantastic in owners' garages. Hedley claims it worked closely with the Porsche Museum to get all the details right and it demonstrates.

Only 250 of these will be made, and they'll cost £69,500 ($91,406) each. So it isn't cheap, especially for something that isn't road legal. However, for folks who can afford to spend that kind of cash on a track day toy, this seems like a really fun way to do it.

Industry News: Volkwagen’s ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept Sends 362 All-Electric Horsepower to the Front Wheels

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Volkswagen’s EV push in America has skewed practical, for the most part.
  • Polo GTI Clubsport Concept is an all-electric, track-ready, front-wheel drive hot hatch.
  • Polo GTI Clubsport Concept can hit a top speed of 149 mph, and it can accelerate from 0-60 mph in 4.7 seconds—quicker than a Golf GTI but not quite as quick as a gas-powered Golf R—with the launch control engaged.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Volkswagen’s EV push in America has skewed practical, for the most part. The ID.4 was a generic crossover, so close to an electric take on the Tiguan that VW is actually rebranding it as the ID. Tiguan. And the ID. Buzz, whimsical styling aside, is an electric van—a very expensive electric van. But VW has not abandoned its small, fun hatchback roots in Europe, and the German brand is continuing the celebration of the 50th anniversary of its GTI sub-brand with an EV: the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept, which it will debut at the Essen Motorshow later this month.

It has been revealed that the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept is an all-electric, track-ready, front-wheel drive hot hatch. VW shoehorned an electric drive system intended for larger RWD vehicles into the sub-compact ID. Polo GTI; that gives the concept outputs of 362 horsepower (up to 389 hp in short bursts) and 406 pound-feet of torque, a massive increase from the 223 hp and 214 lb-ft in the standard model.

The ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept can hit a top speed of 149 mph, and it can accelerate from 0-60 mph in 4.7 seconds—quicker than a Golf GTI but not quite as quick as a gas-powered Golf R—with the launch control engaged.

This VW’s body is heavily modified from the standard model, as well. It features a two-door layout instead of four, flared fenders, and an enormous front splitter, diffuser, and rear wing. VW also stripped out the interior for track work by deleting the rear seat and cargo area. The two front seats are Recaro racing bucket seats with five-point harnesses, and the interior also has an integrated Tornado Red roll bar.

Sadly, this is just a concept for now. Volkswagen has not committed to building an ID. Polo GTI Clubsport, and even if the brand did, it would be unlikely to be offered in the American market. VW did reveal a very cool ID. GTI concept back in 2023, which it has claimed will be more fun than the combustion-powered GTIs. Breaking: Two-Thirds of Dementia Content On TikTok Is Misleading, Researchers Say

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1024 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A fresh survey suggests that about two-thirds of dementia advice videos on TikTok are misleading.
  • Of the videos examined, the analysis shows that nearly half contained inaccurate and potentially damaging information.
  • The researchers say that approximately 44% of TikTok creators who share dementia content lack credibility and appropriate qualifications.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A fresh survey suggests that about two-thirds of dementia advice videos on TikTok are misleading.

Of the videos examined, the analysis shows that nearly half contained inaccurate and potentially damaging information.

The researchers say that approximately 44% of TikTok creators who share dementia content lack credibility and appropriate qualifications.

Although misleading dementia content may appear on other social media platforms, this research examined only TikTok content, warranting further investigation.

The survey was commissioned by Homewatch Caregivers and has not been published in a peer-reviewed scientific journal.

A spokesperson for TikTok told Healthline that if health-related content is potentially harmful, it is flagged for removal. The spokesperson added that 99.6% of misinformation deemed violative was proactively removed from the platform in 2026.

It has been revealed that the spokesperson added that TikTok relies on fact-checking and guidance from public health authorities to help assess the accuracy of content. The platform may also apply warning labels to content that cannot be verified as accurate.

Sources indicate that looking to social media for health information is not uncommon. A recent poll reports that 31% of adults in the United States use social media at least once a month to look for health information and advice.

Experts advise seeking information about dementia from trusted sources, such as a primary care doctor and organizations like the National Institute on Aging (NIA) and the Alzheimer’s Association, rather than social media, where content creators who share advice often lack expertise.

“It’s normal to want answers rapidly when you’re caring for someone living with dementia, and a short video from someone who seems to know what they’re talking about can be really convincing,” said lead researcher Jennifer Winarski, senior manager of care operations and quality for Homewatch CareGivers.

Recent findings suggest that “Despite there being some genuinely helpful information out there, you don’t always know whether it’s backed by medical evidence, so we wanted to bring our own expertise to uncover whether popular TikToks can be trusted,” she told Healthline. “We hope our report will encourage people to be a bit more careful about what they act on.”.

For the survey, researchers selected a sample of 500 of the most-watched dementia-related videos on TikTok with hashtags such as:.

Researchers then transcribed the video data to assess its accuracy.

The researchers found that two-thirds (66.4%) of the popular TikTok videos contained misleading information. Of those videos, about half (47.6%) contained potentially damaging misleading dementia information.

“It’s clear that many of the creators mean well, but much of what we saw was personal opinion rather than proven information, and in a few cases, general good health tips were presented as if they were specifically helpful for individuals living with dementia,” Winarski mentioned.

“If families act on that, they could end up spending time and money on things that won’t help — and in the worst of cases, it could delay getting the support their loved one really needs,” she added.

Industry observers note that dung Trinh, MD, an internist for MemorialCare Medical Group and chief medical officer of the Healthy Brain Clinic in Irvine, CA, mentioned it’s crucial to be aware of the volume of misleading dementia information on social media. Trinh was not involved in this survey.

Some people may be making decisions about their health based on incomplete, misleading, or incorrect information, he said.

“For example, someone might see a video claiming that a particular supplement can reverse Alzheimer’s disease or that certain memory problems automatically mean someone has dementia,” Trinh stated.

“These messages can lead to unnecessary fear, false reassurance, wasted money, or delays in getting a proper diagnosis.”.

“We are entering an exciting era in Alzheimer’s care, with advances in blood-based biomarkers, earlier detection, and treatments that may slow disease progression in appropriately selected patients,” Trinh continued.

“Getting an accurate diagnosis and receiving timely medical guidance are becoming increasingly crucial.”.

It has been revealed that the researchers examined the content creators behind the TikTok videos included in their analysis. They found that 44% of video creators behind the misleading videos had no relevant qualifications.

Rehan Aziz, MD, vice chair of education in the Department of Psychiatry at Hackensack Meridian Jersey Shore University Medical Center and associate professor of psychiatry and neurology at the Hackensack Meridian School of Medicine in New Jersey, said that content creators offering dementia advice should have relevant qualifications. Aziz wasn’t involved in the survey.

“Start by looking at the creator’s profile for a full name and a specific credential, such as MD, DO, PhD, or RN, along with a specialty,” Aziz told Healthline.

“For dementia, the most relevant experts include neurologists, geriatric psychiatrists, geriatricians, neuropsychologists, and nurses, including advanced practice nurses, or social workers who specialize in dementia care.”.

“You can confirm a doctor’s license through your state’s licensing board website and check board certification at certificationmatters.org,” Aziz said.

As of 2020, more than 55 million people worldwide were living with dementia — a neurological condition that negatively affects the brain. Researchers predict this number will hit 78 million by 2030.

The increase in the number of people seeking dementia content online is a reflection of this trend.

Recent findings suggest that when looking for accurate dementia information and guidance, Nestor Beltre, MD, a neurologist with Baptist Health Kenneth C. Griffin Neuroscience Institute, part of Baptist Health South Florida, remarked a great first step is to speak with their primary care physician. Beltre wasn’t involved in the survey.

“Memory changes can occur for many different reasons, and some causes, including vitamin deficiencies, depression, and certain medical conditions, may be treatable,” he told Healthline.

“Early evaluation can help identify what may be contributing to these changes and determine the most appropriate next steps. Depending on the individual’s symptoms, a neurologist, psychiatrist, or neuropsychologist can provide further evaluation and guidance,” Belter continued.

Beltre advised turning to trusted resources such as the Alzheimer’s Association and the National Institute on Aging, which can increase public understanding of memory-related conditions and available treatment options.

“The most important message is that patients and families have resources available to help them better understand and manage cognitive health,” he mentioned.

After taking delivery of its first Orange EV e-Triever electric yard tractor in 2024, NSSL saw the electric light. The tech giant has been moving swiftly to transition its yard tractor fleet to zero emissions, and its efforts haven’t gone unnoticed: NSSL is now being recognized by the 2026 Canadian Clean Fleet Awards.

Toronto’s National Shunt Service, Ltd. (NSSL) added its first electric terminal truck to its trailer-moving operations back in 2024 – and they were impressed enough to rapidly start buying more, putting their Orange e-Triever and Husk-e trucks to work at customers’ warehouses, distribution centers, and factories. The organization has 42 electric trucks working at a number of sites in Canada (up from 27 in June), with plans to have 50 by the end of Q1 2027.

Industry observers note that “(Electric is) part of every customer conversation we’re having today,” says Darren Fitzgerald, NSSL’s chief commercial officer. “If customers aren’t asking about electrification, we are bringing it to the conversation.”.

The manufacturer’s commitment to decarbonization recently made them a 2026 Canadian Clean Fleets Award winner, recognizing their growing role in normalizing battery-electric, zero-emission commercial trucks across Canada.

NSSL used Geotab telematics to track pertinent data of each vehicle, giving what Fitzgerald called, “an essential overview of the entire fleet,” that enabled the firm to compare efficiencies and cost, as well as the ability to plan ahead.

“The data allows us to identify potential maintenance complications before they result in an outage,” he explains. “Just as importantly, it gives us the analytics to understand idle time, fuel and energy consumption, utilization, and overall operating efficiency.”.

If NSSL’s experience is anything like many, many, many others, they’ll find that the case for electrification is stronger than ever.

In a recent development, hyundai and Kia have some of the strongest hybrid lineups on the market. Why did it take so long for Genesis to get there?

Hyundai and Kia hybrids are printing money. Hybrids now account for 29% of all Hyundai sales, a proportion that has grown rapidly over the last few years. But Genesis has so far been left out of the hybrid sales bonanza. No longer. Genesis revealed the G80 and GV80 hybrids on Wednesday, finally entering the fast-growing market for premium hybrids.

In a recent development, the G80 and GV80 are the Genesis brand’s mid-size sedan and SUV, respectively. The G80 competes against cars like the BMW 5 Series and Mercedes E-Class and was—until recently—offered with a fully electric powertrain. That was canned after slow sales, and the GV80 SUV has always been internal-combustion only.

In a recent development, both models come standard with a 2.5-liter turbocharged gas engine and offer twin-turbo V-6 engines as performance upgrades. The new hybrid system will slot between these two powertrains. It adds a parallel hybrid setup to the 2.5-liter turbocharged powertrain, delivering a combined total of 347 horsepower. The top-trim V6 produces 375 hp, for reference.

In a recent development, genesis says the GV80 Hybrid is 24% more efficient than the four-cylinder gas model. For that G80 Hybrid, that number is 30%. Final fuel economy ratings are still to come, but that’s a sizable improvement given the extra power it comes with. And like their gas-powered siblings, all G80s and GV80s come with all-wheel-drive.

All G80 and GV80 Hybrids come standard with all-wheel drive.

According to recent reports, kind of. The 2.5T turbo-hybrid combo is used in other Hyundai products like the Palisade Hybrid, but it is among the newest, most sophisticated powerplants in the company’s stable. But the G80 and GV80 do get some Genesis-exclusive hardware. The Genesis hybrids are the first Hyundai Motor Group (HMG) hybrids to feature liquid-cooled batteries. The vast majority of traditional hybrids use small batteries that are passively air-cooled, but as we know from larger EV batteries, active cooling systems are great for long-term stability. Genesis claims the cooling system also allows it to take advantage of more of the battery’s energy.

Fundamentally, though, the powertrain should feel similar to existing Hyundai and Kia hybrids. Unlike Honda and Toyota hybrids, HMG hybrids still use traditional transmissions rather than e-CVTs. The G80 and GV80 use a seven-speed automatic, rather than the eight-speed auto that’s employed on the gas models.

The new models offer a “Stay” mode that allows you to run the HVAC and radio for extended periods without firing the gas engine, too, and an EV mode for a limited amount of engine-off cruising.

If you want something that’s more similar to an EV driving experience, Genesis already makes two smaller electric SUVs, the GV60 and Electrified GV70. A third one, the stunning GV90, is coming soon.

But if you want something like a plug-in hybrid, you’ll have to wait for the tech giant’s extended-range electric vehicles (EREVs). EREVs—which use gasoline engines purely as generators, with no direct mechanical between the engine and wheels—are coming in 2027, Genesis confirmed at the debut event. The company says they will offer over 640 miles of combined range. EREV fans will have to wait for further details.

The rear seat of the top-trim Genesis G80 Hybrid.

But if you’re a pure hybrid fan, Genesis finally has a couple of real options. Pricing, trim details, and on-sale dates are still to come. Expect to hear more details next year.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • GM claims the pilot participants will be its first EV drivers in California to export power from their cars to their homes.
  • Chevy, GMC, and Cadillac EV drivers can use time-of-use energy management to take advantage of lower rates and may be paid for participating in eligible demand-response events.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, GM Energy and WeaveGrid are launching a vehicle-to-grid (V2G) pilot that will let select Southern California Edison (SCE) customers send electricity from their EV batteries back to the grid. Eligible drivers could get more than $16,000 in help with equipment and installation, and earn money when the grid needs their power.

GM claims the pilot participants will be its first EV drivers in California to export power from their cars to their homes. Through the California Energy Commission, eligible customers in SCE’s Emergency Load Reduction Program can get up to $8,000 toward a GM Energy V2H system and up to $8,099 toward eligible installation costs, including connecting the system to the grid.

Chevy, GMC, and Cadillac EV drivers can use time-of-use energy management to take advantage of lower rates and may be paid for participating in eligible demand-response events. How much they save or earn depends on their rate blueprint, electricity use, and participation.

GM already offers managed charging through 13 utilities, and each program varies by utility.

Industry observers note that an EV battery stores direct current (DC), and your house and the grid use alternating current (AC). GM’s current home backup system uses a wall-mounted inverter to convert the power. With AC bidirectional charging, the car’s onboard inverter does the job. Moving that work into the car could make the equipment on your garage wall simpler and cheaper to install.

According to recent reports, not in CA, but we use solar, time of use, and EVs to minimize our energy costs. We’re not feeding power back to the grid from our cars, but the combo of TOU, solar and EVs does allow us to reduce costs significantly. Solar covers all the expensive peak power, I have the cars start charging early enough to use any extra solar, and the rest is off peak at half cost.

Sources indicate that GM is joining CharIN‘s North American AC V2G task force, which is working to align technical standards, equipment certification, and utility approval requirements. In Southern California, the pilot will give GM and its partners a look at how the process works for drivers, from signing up and getting the hardware installed to getting utility approval and sending power back.

#63831. Early Americans spent over 10 hours making a single pumpkin pie

Early Americans spent over 10 hours making a single pumpkin pie

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1313 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, it’s the late 1700s, and a pumpkin sits on a colonial kitchen table.
  • It seems like an absurd amount of work for dessert.
  • According to recent reports, for generations, cooks solved the problem with heat and muscle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, it’s the late 1700s, and a pumpkin sits on a colonial kitchen table. The flesh has been cooked until soft. But the hard part is still ahead. To turn the pumpkin into pie, the cook must mash it, scrape it, and force it through a sieve, separating smooth pulp from stubborn strings and fibers. There is no can of pumpkin puree. No food processor. Just the pumpkin, rudimentary kitchen tools, and a lot of elbow grease. The work could take hours, all for an eight-person dessert. An 1876 Newly introduced England cookbook, for example, instructed cooks to simmer pumpkin for six to eight hours, stirring frequently, before rubbing it through a colander.

It seems like an absurd amount of work for dessert. Pumpkin flesh doesn’t naturally break down into a silky puree. Cooking softens its tissues, but turning the squash into smooth filling requires additional mechanical work.

According to recent reports, for generations, cooks solved the problem with heat and muscle. Eventually, factories took over the work of cooking and processing pumpkins into puree. But the solution didn’t stop there. Growers also turned to pumpkin varieties with naturally smoother, less fibrous flesh, making the job easier before the squash even reached the factory.

Pumpkin was an important food in North America long before Thanksgiving became a national holiday. Indigenous peoples cultivated and prepared the squash in many forms, and European colonists adopted pumpkins as a plentiful crop. Colonists adapted their own pie-making traditions to the abundant squash, incorporating pumpkin into sweet and savory pies. By the 17th century, recipes for pumpkin-filled pies were appearing in English cookbooks.

According to recent reports, in 1796, the first known American cookbook, Amelia Simmons’s American Cookery, included a recipe for “Pompkin Pudding” made with cooked pumpkin, milk, eggs, and spices. Before the pumpkin could be combined with the other ingredients, the recipe called for it to be strained, separating fine pulp from tougher material.

According to recent reports, thanksgiving didn’t take shape as a national tradition until the mid-19th century. Pumpkins were harvested in the fall and could be stored through the colder months, making them a natural ingredient for a holiday associated with the autumn harvest.

The story of the Pilgrims sitting down with Native Americans for the first Thanksgiving has some truth to it, too. In 1621, English colonists and members of the Wampanoag people did gather for a three-day harvest celebration. But the friendly, feel-good version passed down in schoolbooks leaves out a much more complicated history of colonialism and conflict.

It wasn’t until over two centuries later that Sarah Josepha Hale, a prominent magazine editor, campaigned for decades for a national holiday, and, in 1863, President Abraham Lincoln proclaimed a national “day of Thanksgiving.” She believed a shared day of gratitude, centered on family and community, could help unite a country increasingly divided by political conflict.

According to recent reports, hale also helped popularize the foods associated with the holiday, promoting a traditional Upcoming England Thanksgiving menu through her magazine. Pumpkin pie was already a regional favorite, but as Thanksgiving spread nationally after the Civil War, the dessert became part of the broader American tradition.

Industry observers note that pumpkin pie became increasingly associated with the holiday meal during this era, drawing on its roots in Fresh England’s seasonal cooking traditions. Preparing it remained labor-intensive, and results varied.

Recent findings suggest that industrial food processing offered a solution to the labor-intensive process of making pumpkin pie. Factories could cook and mechanically break down pumpkin in large quantities, producing puree without requiring every household to repeat the tedious process. Canning transformed pumpkin from a seasonal ingredient demanding considerable preparation into a convenient product that could be stored and used when needed.

John Coupland, Ph.D., professor of food science at Penn State, describes the work involved in preparing pumpkin by hand as “astonishing.” Industrial processing made pie filling far more convenient, eliminating the need to cook, mash, and strain a pumpkin from scratch.

It also gave bakers a reliable starting point, helping make pumpkin pie more consistent and cementing its place at the Thanksgiving table.

Industry observers note that making pumpkin puree is more complicated than simply cooking the flesh until soft. Pumpkin cells are surrounded by walls containing materials such as cellulose, hemicellulose, and pectin. Cooking softens the tissue, while mechanical processing breaks it into smaller particles. Together, these processes help determine the puree’s texture and moisture.

In a recent development, the goal is a smooth puree that is neither watery nor full of tough fibers. The pumpkin variety matters, as do the heating conditions and mechanical methods used to break down its flesh.

Modern food processing allows manufacturers to control these variables on a large scale, producing batches with similar textures and moisture levels. That predictability is especially valuable in pumpkin pie, where the filling’s consistency helps determine the finished dessert.

But the food industry found another way to improve the process: start with a pumpkin better suited to the job.

That is where Libby’s, one of the country’s largest canned-pumpkin producers, and the Dickinson pumpkin enter the story.

According to Libby’s, farmer Elijah Dickinson brought special Dickinson pumpkin seeds from Kentucky to Illinois in 1835. The variety became closely associated with commercial pumpkin processing, and Libby, McNeill & Libby acquired Dickinson & Co. in 1929, strengthening the manufacturer’s connection to the crop.

Dickinson pumpkins look different from the bright orange pumpkins sold for carving (often called field pumpkins). Their tan skin matters less to processors than the dense flesh beneath it. Relatively high in solids and sugars, Dickinson pumpkins are particularly well-suited to puree.

Sources indicate that many carving pumpkins, by contrast, have stringier flesh that makes them harder to process into a smooth puree. Coupland explains that they are not ideally suited to commercial food production because their fibers can be difficult to break down.

According to recent reports, coupland describes Dickinson puree as having a “smooth, even texture,” adding that it means you won’t be “picking fibers out of your teeth.” Rather than trying to eliminate the stringiness of a carving pumpkin, processors can start with a variety whose natural characteristics make the job easier. The raw material itself becomes part of the technology.

Libby’s helped bring this approach into American kitchens through its canned-pumpkin business, pairing a suitable variety with industrial processing to deliver consistent puree to home bakers.

In a recent development, interestingly, Dickinson pumpkins belong to Cucurbita moschata, a species that includes several varieties of winter squash. Many familiar carving pumpkins belong to Cucurbita pepo. Botanically, the distinction between pumpkin and squash is largely a matter of common usage rather than a strict scientific boundary. The FDA permits certain sweet, golden-fleshed squashes to be labeled as pumpkin in canned products, reflecting the longstanding overlap in how the terms are used in the food trade.

Recent findings suggest that for pumpkin pie, what matters most is the flesh inside: how it tastes, how it breaks down, and how consistently it performs. Today’s Thanksgiving cooks no longer needs to work themselves to the bone because the food industry has learned to do the work first.

The Next Generation Of U.S.-Made EV Batteries Is Getting Closer To Reality

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (445 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Insideevs

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that silicon anodes could be the next massive thing in lithium-ion battery tech.
  • On Wednesday, Sila Nanotechnologies announced a fresh multi-year offtake agreement with Panasonic.
  • We've heard a lot about silicon-carbon batteries over the last few months.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that silicon anodes could be the next massive thing in lithium-ion battery tech. A new deal paves the way for those more advanced batteries to be made in the U.S.

On Wednesday, Sila Nanotechnologies announced a fresh multi-year offtake agreement with Panasonic. Sila's role is to supply Panasonic with its silicon-carbon anode material, which the battery giant will use in its U.S. plants to build next-generation battery cells.

We've heard a lot about silicon-carbon batteries over the last few months. Mercedes-Benz bought into the idea, Porsche invested in it too. General Motors is going all-in on the tech, the automaker's battery chief, Kurt Kelty, told us earlier this year. So why the big fuss?

It has been revealed that most lithium-ion batteries use graphite on the anode side. Sila's approach uses silicon, which can hold dramatically more lithium. In theory, that means a more energy-dense battery with no additional weight and faster charging speeds. A win all around.

It has been revealed that but, there is a trade-off in the material. Silicon has a habit of "swelling" as it charges and ages due to the sheer amount of extra lithium it can absorb compared to graphite. Sila notes its Titan Silicon anode solves this problem by reducing overall expansion to something more akin to traditional graphite-based anodes. Its anodes already help power some consumer electronics, like Whoop bands.

Sources indicate that the two companies have been working together to commercialize the tech since 2023 when Panasonic first announced prepares to procure anode material from Sila. Now, Panasonic plans to procure it at scale.

Sila's facility in Washington was completed in later 2025 with the ability to produce around 2 Gigawatt-hours of battery material. That's enough to manufacture around 26,000 BEV batteries annually, based on a typical EV battery size of 75 kWh. In July, it secured funding to ramp production to up to 250 GWh. If all goes well, Sila claims that Panasonic has the option to offtake more than $1 billion in product over time.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that for the uninitiated, Inner Mongolia North Hauler Joint Stock Co., Ltd.
  • The NTE240E packs an absolutely MASSIVE battery pack, with the highest-capacity versions offering up to 4,100 kWh (4.1 MWh) of onboard energy storage.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

NHL may not be a household name, but its all-latest, all-electric NTE240E ultra-class haul track could change that with a 240 ton payload, over 4.1 MWh of battery, advanced regenerative braking, and a world’s first double-gun MCS charging setup.

It has been revealed that for the uninitiated, Inner Mongolia North Hauler Joint Stock Co., Ltd. (NHL) is a Chinese heavy equipment manufacturer specializing in the enormous rigid-frame haul trucks used in open-pit mining operations. Established in 1988, NHL has decades of experience building mining trucks for customers around the world, including some of the industry’s largest diesel-electric hybrids. The brand’s latest NTE240E is different, representing a manufacturer’s real push into battery-electric mining equipment, and it’s powering that push with some seriously ambitious technology.

Let’s start with the battery. The NTE240E packs an absolutely MASSIVE battery pack, with the highest-capacity versions offering up to 4,100 kWh (4.1 MWh) of onboard energy storage. Keeping that much battery topped off is no small task, which is why NHL developed an equally ambitious energy replenishment strategy supporting dual-gun MCS charging, allowing its town-sized battery to go from 20% to 90% in under an hour.

That means operators can take advantage of shift changes and scheduled rest breaks to top off the battery without sacrificing an entire work shift to charging – but even more impressive than the fact that all that juice can be crammed into so big a battery in so little time is the fact that, according to NHL, it can be done at just 25°C (about 77°F).

Plugging in isn’t the only way the NTE240E drinks its juice. NHL’s new dynamic power reception system uses overhead current collectors to supply electricity directly to the truck while it’s climbing loaded mine roads, allowing it to then “ride the brakes” for more energy all the way downhill.

It has been revealed that the combined technologies allow NHL’s operators to keep the massive trucks moving without relying entirely on their onboard batteries. The result is a claimed 15% improvement in energy efficiency over the ultra-class industry average.

Sources indicate that that efficiency turns into savings, which means the economics of running an NTE240E could be just as compelling as the emissions savings – and those are substantial. NHL states each NTE240E can reduce harmful carbon emissions by more than 2,000 tons annually, even as it cuts operating costs by more than 60% compared to a comparably capable diesel.

What’s more, because the significant BEV’s electrical system eliminates the need for engine-related hardware like generators and the maintenance and overhaul costs associated with those components. Taken as a whole, the NHL seems to be a compelling offering … but that’s not for me to say. You guys are the experts – let us know what you think of the fresh NHL NTE240E, in the comments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that we may earn revenue from the products available on this page and participate in affiliate programs. Learn more ›.

I reviewed the StickerPix Print + Cut in October and I have made a ton of stickers ever since. My daughter in college has also chewed through a ton of my paper, which is a glowing recommendation since she hates pretty much everything. You can grab that printer and its Essential Bundle for $249.00 (was $299.00) in the Cricut sale at Amazon. The StickerPix Print, which skips the blade, is $119.00 (was $169.00), which is a great deal if you don’t mind buying pre-cut sheets. The rest of the list covers cutting machines, heat presses and the vinyl, iron-on and cardstock you’ll run through fastest. If you’re into making stuff and crafting, you’ll want to jump on these deals and stock up while you can.

The PopSci Proven sticker printer that cuts its own work.

I tested the Cricut StickerPix Print + Cut in October, and setup took less than 10 minutes. The Essential Bundle is $249.00 (was $299.00). It’s a dye-sublimation printer with a blade inside, so it prints a 4 x 7-inch sheet and then kiss-cuts each sticker without slicing through the backing. A few of my stickers survived an accidental trip through the dishwasher. It only works with Cricut’s own paper and ink packs, so plan on buying refills. It earned a PopSci Proven award, and my full StickerPix Print + Cut review covers the paper costs and the quirks.

The same printing tech without the blade, for $130 less.

The Cricut StickerPix Print drops the cutting blade and $130 of the price. It’s $119.00 (was $169.00). Cricut says it uses the same dye-sublimation printing as the StickerPix Print + Cut, but the stickers come on pre-cut sheets, so the shapes are set before you print. It also turns out 4 x 6-inch photo prints. Pick this one if you mostly want labels, round stickers and snapshots and don’t need custom outlines.

A compact cutter sized for printer-paper sticker sheets.

In a recent development, A sheet of printer paper is 8.5 inches wide, and that’s the width Cricut lists for the Cricut Joy Xtra, which is $129.00 (was $179.00) for Black Friday. The sizing is deliberate. This machine can cut around full-color stickers you’ve printed on a regular inkjet, and Cricut claims it works with more than 50 materials, including vinyl, iron-on and cardstock. Cuts top out at 4 feet long, so it handles labels, cards and T-shirt designs, but big wall decals belong on a larger machine.

A 12-inch cutter that’s smaller than the last Explore.

Cricut says the Explore 5 is 30 percent smaller than the machine it replaced, and it kept the 12-inch cutting width. The Cricut Explore 5 Essential Bundle with digital content is $199.00 (was $249.00). It takes the same 12 x 12-inch mats as earlier Explore and Maker machines. Cricut lists more than 100 compatible materials for it, and it can cut Smart Materials up to 12 feet long without a mat, which is the reason to pick it over a Joy if banners or large decals are in your plans.

A palm-size press for the spots a big one can’t reach.

Shoes, stuffed animals, seams and the gaps between shirt buttons are all bad places for a full-size heat press. The Cricut EasyPress Mini in Raspberry is built for them, and it’s $39.00 (was $49.99). Cricut gives it three heat settings, a ceramic-coated plate, an insulated base to rest it on and an automatic shutoff. It’s also the least expensive machine in this post.

Great horned owl survives 70 miles stuck in a moving truck

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (478 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In March, we reported on a bobcat who endured a four-hour surgery on two broken legs after getting hit and dragged by a car, after her head had gotten stuck in the car’s grill.
  • “This is a very unusual case, as most animals that are hit by a tractor-trailer die due to their injuries or are killed instantly,” Tracie Young, director of Raven Ridge Wildlife Center tells Popular Science.
  • Recent findings suggest that the wildlife center’s team received a voicemail from cargo and freight organization Old Dominion Freight Line, saying that one of their drivers in Pennsylvania had hit an owl.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In March, we reported on a bobcat who endured a four-hour surgery on two broken legs after getting hit and dragged by a car, after her head had gotten stuck in the car’s grill. During a strangely similar scenario, the same wildlife center in Pennsylvania recently treated a great horned owl (Bubo virginianus) who also got jammed in the front of a vehicle. But this one was dragged along for 70 miles.

“This is a very unusual case, as most animals that are hit by a tractor-trailer die due to their injuries or are killed instantly,” Tracie Young, director of Raven Ridge Wildlife Center tells Popular Science.

Recent findings suggest that the wildlife center’s team received a voicemail from cargo and freight organization Old Dominion Freight Line, saying that one of their drivers in Pennsylvania had hit an owl. When they called back, they discovered that the owl was alive and had gotten stuck in the truck’s air dam. The company’s maintenance team was able to remove the owl, but something was clearly wrong with the bird because it couldn’t fly away.

In a recent development, the wildlife team told them to place the injured animal in a dark and quiet place. Ultimately, transport volunteers were able to transfer the owl to Raven Ridge, where the team had waited to receive the patient past the wildlife center’s closing hours. Its feathers were a mess, but the staff was shocked to find no broken wings or legs, nor open wounds. The owl had just injured its left eye.

It has been revealed that but when they called back the next day, “the story got even more incredible,” according to the wildlife center. The driver had felt the collision, but she didn’t know that the owl had gotten stuck on the truck, so she’d continued driving all the way back to the terminal.

According to recent reports, “The distance from the spot where the owl was hit to the terminal was 70 miles,” the team wrote.“The owl was stuck headfirst in the fiberglass air dam for 70 miles at 65 miles per hour. It’s truly the luckiest owl we’ve ever seen.”.

Staff brought the hardy survivor to their vet for an eye exam, which revealed blood and swelling in the injured eye. The wildlife team is now monitoring the bird’s recovery.

“The owl is doing great, and the left eye that sustained the damage is also healing. After we move the owl outside into a flight cage, we will make sure that the owl can sustain flight, that there are no obvious underlying concerns, and that it can find the food placed in its cage,” Young concludes.

The goal is to ultimately release it close to where the collision occurred.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that tesla is now rolling out rides in the Cybercab in Dallas, its second major city after the service launched in Austin in September, the automaker remarked in a post on X Thursday.
  • Sources indicate that the automaker was already serving Dallas with its Model Y robotaxis, but this is the first time the purpose-built Cybercab is joining its fleet there.
  • It has been revealed that in addition to Austin and Dallas, Tesla is presently serving riders in Houston, Fort Worth, Tampa, San Antonio, Orlando, and Miami.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that tesla is now rolling out rides in the Cybercab in Dallas, its second major city after the service launched in Austin in September, the automaker remarked in a post on X Thursday. The driverless taxi can carry up to two passengers at a time and doesn’t have a steering wheel or pedals. Riders can order a Cybercab using the Tesla Robotaxi app on their smartphones.

Sources indicate that the automaker was already serving Dallas with its Model Y robotaxis, but this is the first time the purpose-built Cybercab is joining its fleet there. Tesla’s robotaxi rollout has been heavily concentrated in Texas and Florida, since those two states have fewer regulations, letting Tesla add vehicles and expand its geofenced areas more rapidly than in other states.

It has been revealed that in addition to Austin and Dallas, Tesla is presently serving riders in Houston, Fort Worth, Tampa, San Antonio, Orlando, and Miami. The service also runs in the San Francisco Bay Area, but those vehicles have drivers supervising them due to California’s rules. The two-door Cybercab is only present in Austin and Dallas, with the rest of the cities getting the Model Y.

Sources indicate that CEO Elon Musk has remarked the firm eventually aims to have two million Cybercabs in the U.S. That figure deserves some skepticism, given Tesla’s track record of promising major numbers and failing to deliver them. Tesla also plans to wind down Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Austin next summer to ramp up Cybercab production.

Recent findings suggest that tesla recently said it’s sending out invites to select customers to purchase the Cybercab for private use, but that news raised more questions than it answered. The car won’t operate without a $299 per month autonomy subscription, and it’s unclear how it will meet the Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards. Tesla also plans to roll out a version of the Model Y without a steering wheel and pedals to add to its robotaxi fleet.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that and the global increase came despite falling sales in China.
  • Sources indicate that meanwhile, electric vehicle sales have declined in the United States this year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the conversion of the automotive industry over to electric vehicles, sold as a foregone conclusion by many car brands in the early 2020s, may have largely stalled out in America, but the picture is far different globally. According to data from the Commonwealth Bank of Australia, EVs now account for 31 percent of all passenger vehicle sales.

Recent findings suggest that and the global increase came despite falling sales in China. The major driver of electric vehicle sales has been Europe; European EV sales have risen 37 percent year over year so far in 2026, climbing to 43 percent of the new vehicle sales market. CommBank data also revealed substantial growth rates in countries such as Brazil (EV sales up 164 percent, to a 13 percent market share) and India (EV sales up 76 percent, to a 9 percent market share). Even in Japan, where manufacturers have been notably EV-reticent, sales jumped 80 percent year-over-year to 5 percent of the market.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, electric vehicle sales have declined in the United States this year. According to Cox Automotive data, EV sales made up 6.4 percent of the fresh car market in Q3 of 2026, down from more than 10 percent in Q3 of 2025. Fuel prices have been elevated this year, but that has led Americans to gravitate toward hybrids rather than fully electric vehicles. Total electrified vehicles now account for nearly 25 percent of the American market.

It has been revealed that much of the decline has been a direct result of Trump administration policies. Last year, the U.S. eliminated a $7500 federal tax credit for electric cars, which—due to a commercial vehicle loophole—made them especially cheap for buyers to lease; the 10 percent share of sales in Q3 2025 came from a glut of sales as buyers rushed to take advantage of the tax credits before they expired. Congress is also considering imposing an annual federal tax on electric cars.

According to recent reports, the Trump administration has also effectively eliminated enforcement of America’s CAFE standards, which would have effectively forced manufacturers to sell EVs to avoid hefty fines. American laws and tariffs also effectively prohibit importing affordable Chinese-made EVs, which have been a major reason behind the sales increase in Europe.

In a recent development, excuse me while I go find a hat to eat, because Aptera just sold and delivered its first production car. Nothing against Aptera specifically, but when a organization hangs around for 20 years, while exchanging ownership hands several times without actually producing anything for customers, I start to get skeptical. However, Aptera Motors just did what so many doubters thought it'd never do: It delivered a road-legal production vehicle to one of its first early investors.

In a recent development, aptera calls its early investors "Accelerators," and Accelerator #1 was Martin Hartono, CEO of the Indonesia-based GDP Ventures. While Hartono wasn't on site in Carslbad, California to take delivery of the very first Aptera, a representative from GDP Ventures was there in his place. The matte black "Noir" model will soon be exported for Hartono and it will live outside of the U.S.

It has been revealed that “This is the moment our team has worked toward for years,” mentioned Chris Anthony, Co-CEO of Aptera. “To Accelerator #1, and to every reservation holder and shareholder who believed in this vehicle: thank you. We’re working to complete more vehicles for early customers as soon as possible.”.

“What excites me about Aptera is how innovation can redefine the way we use energy in everyday mobility. By combining solar technology, battery power and an ultra-efficient vehicle design, Aptera offers a compelling solution for people who want to minimize their energy consumption without compromising the ability to travel long distances. As an early believer in Aptera, I am proud to be part of this milestone and to see this vision become a reality,” said Martin Hartono, CEO of GDP Venture.

In a recent development, aptera's hook is that its three-wheeled EVs come with solar roofs designed to harness enough sunlight to add up to 40 miles of range per day. While that won't always be the case, Aptera proved, with third-party verification, that its cars are actually capable of exceeding that in the right conditions. Will that revolutionize electric motoring the way Aptera hopes to? That's yet to be seen, but it does offer a interesting concept for customers who don't have long commutes and leave their car parked outside for most of the day while they work. In addition to plugging in to recharge, doesn't it sound nice to recoup your morning commute mileage with the sun while you're in the office?

Whether this three-wheeled rolling solar panel ends up being a hit or not, and whether Aptera can stick around long enough to become a successful automaker, will take much longer to learn. But actually delivering a production car is a good place to start. Even if Aptera couldn't beat GTA 6 to launch.

Tiny egg-eating snake discovered in Ethiopia

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (370 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Biologists have discovered multiple newly introduced species of egg-eating snakes slithering through the forests near southeastern Ethiopia’s Bale Mountains.
  • “Three other species in this genus are still waiting in line,” Arthur Tiutenko, a study co-author and herpetologist at Germany’s Friedrich-Alexander University of Erlangen–Nuremberg (FAU), mentioned in a statement.
  • Many snakes will snack on an egg if the opportunity presents itself.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Biologists have discovered multiple newly introduced species of egg-eating snakes slithering through the forests near southeastern Ethiopia’s Bale Mountains. Although researchers only described the white-throated egg-eater (Dasypeltis albigularis) in their study recently published in the journal Herpetozoa, they promised that information on additional finds is on the way.

“Three other species in this genus are still waiting in line,” Arthur Tiutenko, a study co-author and herpetologist at Germany’s Friedrich-Alexander University of Erlangen–Nuremberg (FAU), mentioned in a statement.

Many snakes will snack on an egg if the opportunity presents itself. But for a handful of species, it’s all eggs, all the time. These nonvenomous snakes solely eat shelled embryos, and largely exist in Africa and some portions of India. To devour their meals, egg-eating snakes have evolved a set of very clever biological tricks. First, their back bones extend all the way into their esophagus and function like a saw to slice open shells. From there, the snake’s neck muscles contract and funnel the egg contents down its throat. Once finished, the reptile simply spits out the cracked shells.

It has been revealed that however, Tiutenko’s team almost missed D. albigularis entirely. At first glance, the snake looks extremely similar to a species called the montane egg-eater (Dasypeltis atra). A closer inspection revealed some key differences—a patch of white scales extending down its stomach earned its “white-throated” moniker, while the skin between each scale has a distinctly blue shimmer. Other egg-eating snakes can rub their scales to create a rustling noise that startles foes, but only the D. albigularis females do the same—and they do it silently.

Don’t envision python-sized snakes chowing down on chicken eggs though. D. albigularis is less than eight inches long, weighs only 0.05 ounces, and is about as thick as a knitting needle. This means the snakes only have eyes for particularly tiny eggs from various diminutive birds. Luckily, their regional home is full of options.

“That may also be the reason why egg-eating snakes only live in Africa, and in particular in a small area in the southwest corner of the Arabian peninsula,” added Tiutenko.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that volkswagen revealed the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept, an electric pocket rocket with a massive rear wing and 362 horsepower.

We knew Volkswagen was cooking something “really spicy” up after teasing the upcoming GTI hot hatch earlier this week.

Volkswagen released the first-generation Golf GTI in 1976, which essentially defined the hot hatch. To celebrate the brand’s legendary performance badge, a signature of its sporty, practical hatchbacks, VW is entering a fresh era with its first fully electric GTI.

The GTI has been “one of Volkswagen’s great success stories for 50 years,” Volkswagen’s technical development boss, Kai Grünitz, said.

After opening pre-orders for the ID. Polo GTI last month, the brand’s first EV to wear the badge, Volkswagen introduced the Clubsport Concept, a souped-up two-door electric pocket rocket.

Sources indicate that the latest ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept shows “how much more potential there is in the electric GTI world,” according to Grünitz.

It’s based on the production ID. Polo GTI uses the same MEB+ platform, but VW reengineered it with a larger electric motor to pump out more power.

Industry observers note that the Clubsport is powered by a 362 hp (270 kW) front-mounted electric motor (APP550) that’s typically used in the rear of VW’s larger EVs, like the ID. Tiguan and the ID.7. That’s up considerably from the 233 hp (166 kW) and 213 lb-ft of torque of the standard ID. Polo GTI offers.

Thomas Schmall, CEO of Volkswagen Group Components, stated the APP550 motor is “one of the most efficient electric drives in its class.”.

Industry observers note that thanks to an electronically controlled front differential lock (VAQ), Volkswagen remarked, the Clubsport version can sprint from 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 km/h) in 4.7 seconds, beating the standard ID. Polo GTI by a full two seconds (6.8 seconds).

Volkswagen also fine-tuned the adaptive chassis control (DCC) to make it racetrack-ready and added newly introduced ceramic brakes to help slow it down.

It has been revealed that the Clubsport version uses the same 52 kW NMC battery as the ID. Polo GTI, which can provide up to 389 hp (290 kW), Volkswagen said, enabling a top speed of 149 mph (240 km/h).

Sources indicate that on the exterior, the Clubsport is a two-door model rather than a four-door. It’s 100 mm longer than the standard ID. Polo GTI, with each wing flared an additional 50 mm. It also gets a large motorsport splitter up front, a wider rear end, a newly introduced diffuser, and a massive carbon-fiber rear wing.

Inside, the cabin is tailored to the racetrack with a minimalist, stripped-down, two-seater layout. As such, there’s no infotainment system, just a center display to switch between drive modes.

The dash panel, side trims, and other interior elements feature dark ArtVelours microfibre with red topstitching, reinforcing the racetrack-ready interior.

Sources indicate that following the ID. Polo GTI, latest ID.3 GTI, and Golf GTI Edition 50, the new ID. Polo Clubsport is the fourth model to debut this year under the performance badge.

Volkswagen opened pre-orders for the ID. Polo GTI last month, starting at 39,995 euros (about $45,000). In early 2027, Volkswagen will open orders for the ID.3 GTI, the second EV to wear the badge, and its first rear-wheel-drive (RWD) GTI.

And American compact car enthusiasts drool over more unobtanium.

It has been revealed that the tech giant will showcase the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport concept car at the Essen Motor Show next week, starting on November 27.

Volkswagen didn’t confirm plans to launch a production version, but don’t expect it to reach the States.

It has been revealed that the standard VW ID. Polo and GTI are not sold in the US, so the souped-up Clubsport variant likely won’t be either. Hopefully, VW changes its mind and proves us wrong.
